title: YouTube MCP setup
intro: This wizard installs your own YouTube MCP server. The server lets Claude search YouTube, read video transcripts, list channel videos, read comments, and search across all transcripts of one channel. It runs on your own Railway account. You need no YouTube API key. You set one access password for the server. You can add an optional cookie file if YouTube blocks your server. The code comes from the repository keyona-rerev/youtube-mcp-server. It is a Python server built with FastMCP and yt-dlp.

steps.title: Check what you need
steps.instructions:
This product runs one small server for you. Claude connects to it and calls its tools.

You need these accounts:
- A GitHub account. It is free.
- A Railway account. Railway charges for hosting. A small server costs a few dollars each month. Check the Railway price page before you start.
- Claude Code or Claude Desktop on your computer.

You do not need a YouTube API key. The server reads public YouTube pages with a tool called yt-dlp.

You will make one access password for the server in a later step. You will enter it only inside Railway and inside your Claude settings. Never type it into this wizard.
steps.checkbox_label: I have a GitHub account and a Railway account.
steps.verify_hint: You can sign in to github.com and railway.com.

steps.title: Copy the code to your GitHub account
steps.instructions:
Open https://github.com/keyona-rerev/youtube-mcp-server in your browser.

Click Fork, near the top right.

Choose your own account as the owner.

Keep or change the repository name. Then enter the name below.

Click Create fork.
steps.checkbox_label: My fork exists in my GitHub account.
steps.verify_hint: Open {{fork_url}}. You see the files Procfile, README.md and requirements.txt.

steps.title: Create the Railway project
steps.instructions:
Open https://railway.com/new and sign in.

Click Deploy from GitHub repo.

Allow Railway to read your GitHub account if it asks.

Choose {{github_username}}/{{repo_name}}.

Click Deploy Now. Railway starts a first build. The first build can fail or show a warning about the password. This is normal. You fix it in the next steps.

Enter the project name you use in Railway below. You can rename the project in Project Settings.
steps.checkbox_label: The Railway project exists and uses my fork.
steps.verify_hint: Railway shows a service that is linked to {{github_username}}/{{repo_name}}. The repository has a file named Procfile. Railway uses it to start the server.

steps.title: Make your access password
steps.instructions:
The server is public on the internet. The access password stops other people from using it. Make a long random value.

Open a terminal on your computer. Run the command that matches your system. The command prints one line of random text.

Copy that line. Keep it in your password manager. You need it again in two later steps.

Do not paste the password into this wizard.
steps.checkbox_label: I made a password and saved it in my password manager.
steps.verify_hint: Your password is a line of 64 letters and numbers.

steps.title: Add the password in Railway
steps.instructions:
In Railway, open your service. Click the Variables tab.

Click New Variable.

Enter the name shown below.

Paste your own password as the value.

Click Add. Railway offers to deploy. Click Deploy.

Enter the password only here, inside your own Railway account.
steps.checkbox_label: The variable MCP_AUTH_TOKEN is saved in Railway.
steps.verify_hint: The Variables tab lists MCP_AUTH_TOKEN. The value is hidden.

steps.title: Add a cookie file (optional)
steps.instructions:
YouTube sometimes blocks servers that run in data centers. It shows a bot check. A cookie file from a signed-in browser answers the check. Skip this step if you want to try without cookies first. You can come back to it later.

If you add cookies, use a separate Google account that you do not need. Cookies give access to the account they come from.

1. Sign in to YouTube with the separate account in a private browser window.
2. Export the cookies for youtube.com in Netscape format. Use a cookie export extension that you trust.
3. Save the file as cookies.txt.
4. Turn the file into one line of base64 text. Use the command below.
5. In Railway, open the Variables tab. Add the variable named below. Paste the base64 text as the value.
6. Click Deploy.

The server accepts base64 because some screens remove the tab characters that the cookie format needs.

copy.label: Mac or Linux: make base64 text

steps.checkbox_label: I added the cookie variable, or I chose to skip it for now.
steps.verify_hint: If you added cookies, the Railway deploy log later shows the line: cookies: loaded.

steps.title: Open a public address
steps.instructions:
In Railway, open your service. Click the Settings tab.

Find Networking. Click Generate Domain.

Railway shows an address that starts with https://.

Copy the address. Enter it below. Do not add a slash at the end.

Wait until the latest deploy shows Active.
steps.checkbox_label: My service has a public address and the deploy is Active.
steps.verify_hint: The Railway Deployments tab shows the newest deploy as Active.

steps.title: Read the start-up log
steps.instructions:
In Railway, open the Deployments tab. Click the newest deploy. Click View Logs.

Look for these lines:
- yt-dlp: followed by a version number.
- auth: token required.
- cookies: loaded, or cookies: none.

If you see the line that starts with auth: OPEN, the password is missing. Go back to the step Add the password in Railway. Fix it before you go on.
steps.checkbox_label: The log shows auth: token required.
steps.verify_hint: The log shows auth: token required. It does not show auth: OPEN.

steps.title: Test the server from your terminal
steps.instructions:
Run the first command. You must see the word unauthorized and the code 401. This proves strangers cannot use your server.

Run the second command. Replace PASTE_YOUR_OWN_VALUE_HERE with your password. The answer must not be 401. Any other answer shows the password works. The server may answer with a message about the request format. This is normal for a plain test.
steps.checkbox_label: The first test returns 401. The second test does not return 401.
steps.verify_hint: Test one returns 401 and the text unauthorized. Test two returns a different code.

steps.title: Connect the server to Claude
steps.instructions:
Pick the way you use Claude.

Option A: Claude Code. Run the command below in your terminal. Replace the placeholder with your password.

Option B: Claude Desktop. Open Settings, then Developer, then Edit Config. Add the block below inside mcpServers. Replace the placeholder with your password. Keep the word Bearer and the space after it. Save the file. Restart Claude Desktop. This option needs Node.js on your computer.

The server checks a password header on every request. Some Claude web connector screens cannot send a custom header. If you use only Claude on the web, ask ReRev Labs for help.

Enter the password only in your own Claude settings.

copy.label: Option A: Claude Code command
copy.text: claude mcp add --transport http youtube {{mcp_url}} --header "Authorization: Bearer PASTE_YOUR_OWN_VALUE_HERE"

copy.label: Option B: Claude Desktop config block

steps.checkbox_label: I added the server to Claude.
steps.verify_hint: Claude lists a server named youtube with 8 tools.

steps.title: Run your first test
steps.instructions:
Open a new chat in Claude. Paste the first prompt below.

Claude must call the tool get_video_info and show the title of the video.

Then paste the second prompt. Claude must call get_transcript and show text with timestamps.

If the transcript call fails with a message about blocked requests, YouTube is blocking your server address. Add the cookie file from the optional step. Wait a few hours if you made many requests.

The server has 8 tools: search_videos, get_video_info, get_channel_info, get_channel_videos, get_transcript, get_comments, search_transcript and search_channel_transcripts.

copy.label: Test 1
copy.text: Use the youtube tools. Get the video info for https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=dQw4w9WgXcQ

copy.label: Test 2
copy.text: Use the youtube tools. Get the transcript for https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=dQw4w9WgXcQ

steps.checkbox_label: Claude returned video info and a transcript.
steps.verify_hint: Claude shows the video title and transcript lines with timestamps.

steps.title: How to update later
steps.instructions:
The code changes over time. YouTube changes often, and the tool yt-dlp needs updates to keep up. This code asks for the newest yt-dlp build each time Railway builds it.

Open the version history page of this wizard. It lists each version and what to do.

To update, open {{fork_url}} on GitHub. Click Sync fork, then Update branch. Railway builds again by itself. If a build fails, open the Railway logs and read the last lines.

To make Railway rebuild without a code change, open the Deployments tab. Click the three dots on the newest deploy. Click Redeploy.

To find your current version, see the how to find your version text on the history page.
steps.checkbox_label: I know how to update my copy.
steps.verify_hint: You opened the version history page of this wizard.
